Williamsburg Bridge — vertical arrangement evidence — photo review

Give each photograph every category it can actually inform — one view of a tower is often masonry, a cornice and a cable anchorage at once. Tick skip for anything not worth keeping. Untouched photographs stay auto_screened and are treated as weaker evidence.
A photograph can establish what something is made of and how it is arranged. It cannot give a dimension without scale control. Tick a category for what the image shows, not for what you hope to measure from it.
cable profile
An elevation view along the bridge showing a main cable running tower to tower. CTL-102 is a PLACEHOLDER: the model puts the cable low point 15 ft above the top of the stiffening truss and no source says that. Tick this when the frame shows the cable and the deck together clearly enough to see which is higher at midspan. This cannot measure the sag - it can only confirm or contradict the arrangement the placeholder assumes.
cable cradling
The four cables converging toward each other near midspan. SRC-004 says the pairs narrow from 34 ft apart at the anchorages to 4 ft at midspan, and the model draws exactly that. It is the feature that makes this bridge look like itself, and it is currently drawn on one tertiary source alone.
tower top and saddle
The top of a main tower where the cables cross it. CTL-106 saddle height is a placeholder. SRC-004 gives plan dimensions and Structure Magazine says the saddles are 19 ft long, but nothing read states how tall one stands above the tower top, and the model guesses. A photograph settles how much saddle is visible above the steelwork.
anchorage
Where a main cable enters an anchorage. CTL-103 and CTL-104 are both placeholders: the deck elevation at the anchorage and the anchorage top elevation are guesses. A view showing the cable, the anchorage top and the deck in one frame constrains both, without measuring either.
stiffening truss in elevation
A side-on view of the stiffening truss. SRC-007 gives 67 ft wide and about 40 ft deep and says it is pinned at each main tower (OQ-011). The model draws top and bottom chords only, with no web members, and nothing has confirmed the truss form.
side span intermediate tower
The side span between a main tower and its anchorage. SRC-007 says three intermediate towers per side span, now CTL-039 at grade A, but the model does not draw them yet. CNF-013 is still open: SRC-010 calls these 'steel arches' and SRC-004 calls them trusswork on intermediate towers. This is the category that settles which.
material close-up
Riveted steel, masonry pier facing, cable wrapping, deck surface. Several MAT- rules still rest on a single tertiary source.
period or construction view
Anything showing the bridge under construction or before the 1990s reconstruction. The cable profile TODAY is not the profile as built: SRC-007 states the dead load has increased and 'the profile has flattened', and that suspenders were re-jacked to restore it. A modern photograph is therefore evidence about the modern bridge only, and this category is how that distinction stays visible.
context
A good overall view that settles no single component. Useful beside the model, weak as evidence.
